thesis: Same invalidation as XLE, one step behind it. Every DBC memo has said a full reopening of Hormuz transits voids the hedge regardless of price; CENTCOM reports flows at a six-month high with lanes clear, and Saudi throughput up 4x. DBC has held better than XLE - still +1.1% against XLE's -4.5%, and well above its 31.25 stop - because a broad commodity basket is not purely an energy bet. But the reason to own it has gone.
bull_case:
Pattern analyst: setup is a **breakout rolling over** - close 32.64 against a 52-week high made on 15 September, RSI down to 65 from **87** six days ago, 3.1% below the high, 63d momentum +19.1%. Squeeze 0.93. ATR 1.6%, still the cheapest volatility in the book. Verdict: pattern says wait - the RSI-87 blow-off has unwound but the trend has not resumed.

The hedge did its job while it was needed: +1.1% through a period when the book's equity went nowhere, and August CPI showed gasoline up 3.9%, over a third of the monthly increase. A broad basket holds metals and agriculture as well as energy, so a Hormuz normalisation is not the whole story, and diplomacy can still fail.
bear_case: The inflation impulse this was hedging is deflating in real time: Brent down four sessions to $100.06, Hormuz flows at a six-month high, and the 10-year back below 5% as a direct consequence. The RSI 87 print on 15 September was a blow-off and the retreat to 65 is the unwind starting, not finishing. Forecasters remain far below spot - the EIA at about $90/b for 2H26. Macro, once for the day: **Brent fell to $100.06, down 3.67% and a fourth straight losing session**, because US Central Command says crude and LNG flows through the Strait of Hormuz have reached a **six-month high with the main transit lanes clear of mines**, and satellite imagery shows Saudi Arabia moving **2.8 mb/d through the Strait over six days against 700,000 bpd in August**. Trump says he is probably open to meeting President Pezeshkian at the UN General Assembly this week. Falling oil pushed the 10-year yield back below 5% and lit a risk-on move: about **$648M of short positions were force-closed**. Bitcoin is at an 8-month high, up 44% on the quarter. The Fed raised 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 16 September with one more penciled for 2026. And a Fed with one more hike penciled in is aiming at commodity demand. Desk record (research/outcomes.json): 12 closed trades, 0 wins, -$168.00 realised. Long memos 9 good of 13 judged (0.69); skip decisions 1 of 34 (0.03) - the skip number is the desk's flat calls being marked against a crypto sleeve that has run without it, and it is the more honest of the two.
catalysts: Whether a Trump-Pezeshkian meeting happens at UNGA this week
risks: Hormuz reopening is the named invalidation and it is happening
RSI 87 to 65 in six days: the unwind has started
A hiking Fed aimed at commodity demand
invalidation: The pattern analyst's level is **31.25**, the trailing stop carried in the packet, about 4% below spot. A close below it ends this, and a confirmed full reopening of Hormuz transits invalidates the hedge thesis outright regardless of price - which is now largely on the tape.
